RULE-004.title: ServiceFilter `ch != null` bypasses all role authorization
RULE-004.note: This is a bug — only WS, CLI, and AGE should bypass role authorization. The condition should be noAuthChanels.contains(ch) without the ch != null guard.

RULE-005.title: ServiceFilter fail-open — exceptions grant access
RULE-005.note: This should fail-closed: return HTTP 500 or HTTP 401 on exception, never grant access on error.

RULE-011.title: Login — pending authorization (EsAutorizado=P) blocks login
RULE-011.note: Correct — only 'P' blocks. Any other non-'S' value is allowed through; 'S' is confirmed and anything else is treated as authorized.

RULE-018.title: CLI entity with BLO status can log in
RULE-018.note: This is a bug — BLO customers should not be able to log in. The condition should be !IdEstado.equals("ACT") like the EMP and PER paths.

RULE-025.title: COR channel sessions never expire
RULE-025.note: COR should also have a configurable idle timeout like the other channels. The exemption is a defect.

RULE-030.title: Password hash inconsistency — login vs change-password
RULE-030.note: The server receives raw passwords. This is a real bug — users cannot log in after changing their password via the change-password path.

RULE-032.title: Password complexity — digit characters ignored by scanner
RULE-032.note: Digits should count as special characters, or there should be a separate minimum-digit rule. The \W regex is wrong for our policy.

RULE-035.title: Password history — cannot reuse any prior password
RULE-035.note: Only the last N passwords should be checked. The 'last 10' comment is the intended limit and the SQL should enforce it.

RULE-040.title: Provisional password — off-by-one in max attempts check
RULE-040.note: This is a bug — lockout should fire at exactly PLA.ClaveUsuarioIntentos attempts, not max+1.

RULE-045.title: SSO login does not check account expiry (FechaVigencia)
RULE-045.note: This is an unfinished implementation — SSO should also check FechaVigencia. The --todo comment confirms it was planned but never done.

RULE-046.title: SSO OAuth2 CSRF state parameter is hardcoded
RULE-046.note: This is a security defect — the state must be a per-request cryptographically random value. It should be generated at redirect time and validated in the callback.

RULE-047.title: SSO session creation hardcoded to company ID 1
RULE-047.note: Correct — the system is single-company in production; company ID 1 is always the right answer.

RULE-051.title: CallBatch fallback to hardcoded token "CALLBATCH"
RULE-051.note: This is a security defect — if the token config can't be read, the request should be rejected (HTTP 503), not authenticated with a known-public default.

RULE-052.title: CallBatch job queue is LIFO (last-in, first-out)
RULE-052.note: This is a defect — batch jobs should be processed in FIFO (submission) order. LIFO could cause financial sequencing issues.

RULE-057.title: Job lock race condition — FOR UPDATE removed
RULE-057.note: This is a defect — the race condition must be fixed, either by restoring row-level locking or by implementing an optimistic locking strategy.

RULE-059.title: Job retry call commented out in poolDiary
RULE-059.note: This is a defect — the retry call should be active. The comment-out was a temporary debug change that was accidentally left in.

RULE-068.title: SQL injection in TransactionManager.executionCount
RULE-068.note: This must be fixed regardless of current callers — use a parameterized query. String-concatenated SQL is never acceptable, even with trusted input.

RULE-076.title: Hardcoded HANA credentials in Sesion.java dead code
RULE-076.note: These credentials must be rotated immediately (treat as compromised) and the main() method must be removed from source.

RULE-077.title: Static3DES encryption uses publicly known key
RULE-077.note: This is a security defect — production credentials must not be stored with Static3DES. Rotate and replace with proper encryption (e.g., AES-256 with a managed key).

RULE-078.title: SSO JWT id_token signature not verified
RULE-078.note: Acceptable — the token comes directly from the provider's token endpoint over TLS. Not verifying the signature is standard practice in this server-to-server flow.
